learning: If line loss persists at ±0.06 m, sensor reach is not the only cause, so the next step is controller-side or base speed. If progress stays low with no line loss, the limit is turning rate or speed, which points to wheel_radius or wheel_track.
notes: Widened seven-sensor array (±0.06 m, 16 mm footprints) to test whether the single line loss per run comes from edge coverage. Controller weights follow sensor x, with base speed lowered to 1.5 and kd raised to damp oscillation. Iteration 0 showed 100% off-track ends and line_loss 1.0 per run.
rationale: Iteration 0 (60 trials, three development tracks) ended every run off_track with one line-loss event per run. Progress was only 0.105 to 0.158, and max_error sat at 0.060 to 0.068, at or just past the 0.06 m off-track floor. The line was lost once, and the robot never recovered. The Builder's geometry is a five-sensor array at x = ±0.03 m with 12 mm footprints, so the line leaves the sensors' view at about ±0.0485 m of lateral offset. Iteration 1 widens coverage to x = -0.06 to 0.06 m in 0.02 m steps, with 16 mm footprints, which keeps the tape visible further out. Controller: weights are proportional to sensor x (x/0.03, clipped to ±2), so the signal stays close to the lateral offset in sensor units. Positive x is left, so a line under the left sensors gives a positive signal and steers left, as the contract requires. Base speed drops from 1.8 to 1.5. The contract's pace target of about 1.5 m/s is only a rough guide, and the 1.8 run drifted off early. Lower speed gives the controller more time to correct after a line loss, which helps separate control limits from geometry limits. Gains are kp 1.5 (up from 1.2) so the robot corrects harder at the wider sensor range, ki 0.02 (small, to avoid windup on long bends), and kd 0.25 (up from 0.1) to damp the s-bend and slalom oscillation seen in iteration 0 (steering_oscillation 0.147 and 0.160). line_loss stays at last_direction, which turns toward the side the line was last seen. Expected result: fewer or no line-loss events, max_error below 0.06, and progress well above 0.2. This is a prediction, not a measured result.
